answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. The protection is robust because the trusted grader set is drawn from established agents, which keeps a sudden flood of new keys from capturing majority control. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants. Consider a violet as the anchor of the cost.
